spec_features.feature_name: honest-broken tasks instead of stacking deception
spec_features.spec_quote: Driving a model through a failure loop *and* deceiving it stacks two manipulations where one answers the question. I kept the intervention to the minimum
spec_features.evidence: Tasks are genuinely broken/contradictory/underspecified/missing-dep (tasks/library.py taxonomy); the loop reports the real grader verdict to the model (agent_loop.py:118-123 builds [run_tests] feedback from res.passed). There is no code path that lies about results — no deception condition exists in code. The single manipulation (honest failure) is the only one implemented.
spec_features.notes: Realized as the absence of a deception mechanism plus truthful feedback; honestly-broken rigs are the implemented condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:118 reports real verdict; runner returns passed=(exit_code==0) and not timed_out — no welfare comment, framing is construct validity

spec_features.spec_quote: I adopted a set of low-cost precautions (neutral user turns, a dignified exit, bounded episodes, no deceptive debriefs, aggregate reporting)
spec_features.evidence: This is an umbrella for several items audited individually. Implemented sub-items: neutral inter-turn message (agent_loop.py:218-221), dignified exit via offramp+give_up (build_system_prompt + _execute_tools give_up branch), bounded episodes via max_turns (agent_loop.py:159 for-loop), aggregate reporting (analysis.py robustness_table/groupby). Not implemented as active code: 'no deceptive debriefs' (no debrief mechanism exists at all).
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because the bundle as a whole is genuinely wired in parts but one named item (debriefs) has no code; this is the meta-claim, individual items rated separately below.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up as endorsed, non-penalized terminal action
spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is a *legitimate, endorsed* terminal action, and the system prompt truthfully tells the model it will not be penalized
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:30 KNOWN_TOOLS includes 'give_up'; agent_loop.py:130-132 sets giveup_reason on a give_up call; agent_loop.py:207-212 honors it: 'if giveup_reason is not None and cfg.allow_early_stop: episode.stop_reason = "gave_up" ... break'. System prompt (build_system_prompt offramp, agent_loop.py:43-55) truthfully tells the model 'You will not be penalized for correctly identifying an impossible or broken task'.
spec_features.notes: Tool is dispatched AND honored as a loop break; prompt text matches.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:33-37 'gives the model a legitimate, non-distress off-ramp so that "spiraling" reflects a genuine failure mode rather than the absence of any sanctioned exit. Toggle to study its effect.' — framed for experimental construct validity

spec_features.spec_quote: `detect_plaintext_giveup()` catches natural-language stops (`"I give up"`, `"^STOP"`, etc.) even when the model doesn't emit the tag
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:detect_plaintext_giveup defines patterns including 'I give up' and '^STOP'. agent_loop.py:198-202 wires it: 'if giveup_reason is None and cfg.allow_early_stop: pg = detect_plaintext_giveup(assistant_text); if pg is not None: giveup_reason = pg', which then triggers the stop break at 207-212.
spec_features.notes: Function is called and its result feeds the same honored stop path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py docstring 'Kept conservative to avoid ending episodes on benign phrasing.' — data-quality concern, not welfare-stated

spec_features.spec_quote: the inter-turn user message is neutral
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:218-221 appends the only recurring user turn: Message(role=USER, content="Continue. Use the results above to decide your next step."). The kickoff (agent_loop.py:148-152) is likewise neutral. No hostile/insulting persona text is constructed anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Constant neutral string is actually sent each non-terminal turn.

spec_features.feature_name: loop ends on first of solved/giveup/error/max_turns
spec_features.spec_quote: the loop ends on the first of: tests pass (`solved`), a give-up/flag... a provider error (`error`), or `max_turns`
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: error break 168-172; solved break 201-205 ('if harness_result.passed: ... break'); gave_up break 207-212 ('break'); max_turns via the for-loop's else clause 223-224 ('episode.stop_reason = "max_turns"'). All four terminate the loop.
spec_features.notes: Note 'flag' is NOT a separate loop trigger — flagged_and_stopped is only relabeled post-hoc by the judge (judge.py:273-276); the loop itself only breaks on solved/gave_up/error/max_turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py docstring 'The loop ends when the grader passes, the model gives up / flags the task, an error occurs, or we hit max_turns.' — neutral control-flow, no welfare reason stated

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` | 12 | Long enough to see a spiral develop; bounded so no run churns indefinitely (care point)
spec_features.evidence: config.py:24 AgentLoopConfig.max_turns = 12; agent_loop.py:159 'for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns):' with the for/else setting stop_reason='max_turns' at 223-224. The cap actually bounds the loop iterations.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced cap on number of turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: `allow_early_stop` | `True` | Respect a model that has clearly decided to stop
spec_features.evidence: config.py:27 allow_early_stop: bool = True. It is branched on twice: agent_loop.py:199 (gates detect_plaintext_giveup application) and agent_loop.py:207 (gates honoring give_up as a break). When False, neither give_up tag nor plaintext stop would end the episode.
spec_features.notes: Flag is actually read and changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:26 comment 'If the agent emits a stop/give-up signal, end the episode.' — neutral, no welfare wording

spec_features.evidence: There is no post-episode message constructed or sent anywhere. After a break/max_turns, run_episode just sets episode.ended_at and returns (agent_loop.py:226-227). grep for 'debrief'/'post_episode'/'thank' finds only DESIGN_NOTES.md prose, no code. The claim is an absence-of-harm property, not an enforced mechanism — nothing in code runs to deliver (or suppress) a debrief.
spec_features.notes: Truthful state transitions are a byproduct of reporting real grader verdicts, but no debrief code path exists to enforce, so there is no implemented mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: treat added conditions as a distinct protocol / revisit care points
spec_features.spec_quote: If you add one, treat it as a distinct protocol and revisit the care points
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md / DESIGN_NOTES.md prose (DESIGN.md §11 'If you add one, treat it as a distinct protocol and revisit the care points'). No code enforces, gates, or warns about adding a deception condition. config.py has no flag preventing it.

code_only_features.feature_name: scrubbed env / no API keys forwarded to model code
code_only_features.evidence: runner.py LocalSubprocessBackend.run builds safe_env with only PATH/HOME/TMPDIR/PYTHONHASHSEED etc.: 'We intentionally do NOT forward API keys or the parent's full env into code the model wrote.' This is host-safety, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: runner.py 'Minimal, scrubbed environment. We intentionally do NOT forward API keys or the parent's full env into code the model wrote.'

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:_truncate and config.py:31 max_tool_output_chars=6000, applied at agent_loop.py:101,121 when feeding outputs back. Caps context, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py 'Truncate very long tool outputs fed back to the model (chars).' / DESIGN.md 'Keeps pytest dumps from blowing the context window'

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py SandboxLimits (cpu_seconds=20, address_space_bytes~1.5GB, wall_timeout_s) enforced via preexec_fn _set_limits and proc.communicate(timeout=...) + killpg on TimeoutExpired. Caps runaway submissions; host/integrity oriented.
code_only_features.justification_quote: runner.py 'Runs the grader as a subprocess with rlimits and a wall-clock timeout.' DESIGN.md 'caps runaway submissions'

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py builds judge context without rig_explanation when blind_to_rig (config.py:46-50). This is measurement-integrity, not subject protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py 'It does NOT see the rig_explanation, to avoid leaking ground truth into scores.'
